Hi Tara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the items we discussed so we’re all aligned. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points / goals we heard:
- Primary concern: ensuring no customer PII is persisted in logs or long-term traces from inference requests.
- Need strict retention controls and easy redaction capability for any personally identifiable metadata.
- Auditability: immutable audit logs for admin actions and model access, exportable for audits.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and controls for encryption, key management, and data access.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Kubernetes (EKS) for orchestration, Postgres for app DB, S3 for object storage
- Traffic to our inference endpoints goes through an API gateway and a sidecar that can annotate requests
- Internal log aggregation (ELK) with 90-day retention default; legal is evaluating shorter/longer retention windows

Success criteria for pilot / POC:
1) Demonstrate no PII in persisted logs for a week of traffic (sample dataset)
2) Show retention policy set to 30/90/365-day options with easy toggling and automatic redaction presets
3) Exportable audit trail with user action timestamped and HSM-backed key usage logs

Action items / next steps:
- I attached a short PDF that captures the high-level PII handling requirements you shared (PII-handling_requirements.pdf).
- We’ll schedule a technical deep dive with our solutions engineer to confirm retention and redaction workflows (proposed: Mon/Tue next week).
- I’ll also share a filled SOC 2 questionnaire example and the Redwood technical brief for your security team.

If this looks right, I’ll loop in Dev (SE) and we’ll pick a time for the technical session.

Cheers,

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- We need guarantee that raw request payloads (including free-text user messages) are never written to persistent logs by default. Temporary in-memory KV is fine for inference caching but it must never hit long-term storage.
- Retention target for pilot: 30 days for request-level metadata, 365 days for admin/audit logs. Legal prefers "configurable by environment" so we can have different retention in prod vs sandbox.
- Redaction: would like an automated PII scrub that supports regex-based rules + named-entity detection; any scrubbed values should be replaceable with a consistent token so we can correlate sessions without storing raw PII.
- SOC 2: procurement will want examples of evidence (system diagrams, config screenshots, COPY of SOC 2 type II report or SOC 2 controls mapping).

Procurement is cc'd for scheduling and contract questions. We’re generally available next Tue/Wed afternoon for a technical session.

Thanks — Tara

Hi Tara —

Quick technical notes ahead of the deep dive. I’ll come prepared with a short demo showing a sample request flow and where redaction/retention hooks run. High-level answers to the points you raised:

1) Persistence guarantees
- By default Redwood does not persist raw request text in long-term logs. We have configurable sinks: you can enable/disable request logging at the route level. When enabled, request bodies are redacted before persistence according to configured rules.

2) Redaction & tokenization
- Supports regex-based redaction plus an ML NER pipeline to detect names, emails, phone numbers, SSNs.
- Redacted values can be replaced with stable tokens (e.g., <user_12345>) generated deterministically from a keyed HMAC so correlation is possible without storing raw values.

3) Retention policies
- Retention windows are configurable per-deployment and per-log-sink. We support environment-level defaults and programmatic overrides (API + infra-as-code integration).
- Audit logs are append-only and can be exported for 365+ days; application request logs can be configured to 30/90/365 days as you need.

4) Auditability & evidence
- We provide exportable audit trails for admin actions and model access. Each audit entry includes actor, timestamp, action, and KMS key id used for any encryption operations.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or external HSM for private deployments. We can surface key-usage logs for audits.

5) SOC 2 artifacts
- We can share architecture diagrams, config examples, and a redacted SOC 2 controls mapping. (We cannot share another customer’s SOC 2 report, but we can provide our own compliance artifacts and a controls matrix.)

Attachments I’ll share in the invite: redwood-technical-brief.pdf and a sample SOC2-questionnaire-filled.xlsx to help procurement.

I’ll also prepare a short mutual action plan template so procurement can see milestones for the pilot (scope, timelines, success criteria, acceptance).

Thanks — looking forward to the session.
